{"text":"Objective:
Design a progressive, 5-page Graphical User Interface (GUI) for a ROS 2 robotics application. The design must be highly professional, industry-standard, and minimalistic.

Global Color Palette & Styling (Strictly Adhere to These Colors):
Based on the reference design, apply this exact color scheme across all pages to ensure consistency:

    Main App Background: Off-white/very light gray (to frame the main content).

    Main Canvas Container: Pure White with a subtle, soft drop shadow.

    Text/Typography: Dark Charcoal (almost black) for maximum readability.

    Logging Panel Background: Light Gray.

    "Back" Button: White with a light gray border and dark text.

    Action Button 1 (Navigation/Dropdown): Vibrant Teal.

    Action Button 2 (SLAM Mapping): Muted Sage Green.

    Action Button 3 (Pause): Soft Cornflower Blue.

    Action Button 4 (Cancel): Soft Coral/Red.

Global UI Requirements (Applies to ALL Pages):

    Universal Back Button: A clean "Back" button (white with a light gray outline) positioned in the top left corner.

    Persistent Logging Screen: A light gray panel anchored at the absolute bottom of the screen (occupying the bottom 20-25%). It resembles a terminal with crisp, dark monospace text.

    No Extraneous Icons: Strictly no battery, Wi-Fi, settings, or OS gear icons. Keep the canvas clean.

Page 1: The Initialization State

    Top Center Heading: Display the text: "Map Selection".

    Main Canvas Layout: Perfectly centered horizontally and vertically (above the logging panel).

    Content:

        A clean heading question: "On which map you want to navigate the Bot"

        Directly below it, a single dropdown menu labeled "Select Map".

        Styling: The dropdown menu should have a white background, a light border, and a Vibrant Teal chevron arrow on the right side.

Page 2: The Mode Selection State

    Top Center Heading: Update to reflect the map (e.g., "Map: Factory\_Floor\_1").

    Main Canvas Layout: Perfectly centered horizontally and vertically.

    Content:

        A clean heading question: "Do you want to do navigation or Mapping"

        Directly below it, two wide call-to-action buttons placed side-by-side.

        Styling:

            Left Button: "Autonomous Navigation" (Fill color: Vibrant Teal, Text: White).

            Right Button: "SLAM Mapping" (Fill color: Muted Sage Green, Text: White).

Page 3: The Navigation Action State

    Top Center Heading: Display the text: "Autonomous Navigation Mode".

    Main Canvas Layout: Split view for data feeds, upper middle alignment.

    Content:

        A clear text prompt directly below the heading: "Give destination pose via RViz".

        Visual Feeds (Side-by-Side):

            Left Frame: Map View (RViz/SLAM) showing a 2D grid and obstacles.

            Right Frame: Live Camera Feed (Gazebo) showing a 3D perspective of the robot.

        Control Buttons: Placed neatly below the visual feeds.

        Styling:

            Left Button: "Pause Navigation" (Fill color: Soft Cornflower Blue, Text: White).

            Right Button: "Cancel Navigation" (Fill color: Soft Coral/Red, Text: White).

Page 4: The Auto Mapping State

    Top Center Heading: Display the text: "Auto SLAM Mapping".

    Main Canvas Layout: Split view for data feeds, filling the center canvas.

    Content:

        Visual Feeds (Side-by-Side):

            Left Frame: Map View (RViz/SLAM) showing a 2D grid and obstacles building in real-time.

            Right Frame: Live Camera Feed (Gazebo) showing the 3D perspective.

        (Note: No manual control buttons are needed on this page, just the live feeds running automatically above the logging panel).

Page 5: The Manual Mapping State

    Top Center Heading: Display the text: "Manual SLAM Mapping".

    Main Canvas Layout: Split view for data feeds with a keyboard guide below them.

    Content:

        Visual Feeds (Side-by-Side):

            Left Frame: Map View (RViz/SLAM).

            Right Frame: Live Camera Feed (Gazebo).

        Keyboard Guide Overlay: Centered at the very bottom of the Main Control Canvas (resting directly above the persistent logging panel).

        Styling for Guide: A sleek, minimalistic visual guide showing keyboard mappings arranged in a cross/D-pad shape (use plain text or subtle light gray key-caps):

            Top: "Press I to move forward"

            Left: "J to rotate left"

            Right: "L to rotate right"

            Center/Bottom: "K to stop"","providerOptions":{}}
